samples.summary: The `adjudication.upheld` counter that applySkipClaims increments is never persisted, so "skipping the same finding twice pages a human" can never fire
samples.evidence: `applySkipClaims` (review-panel.mjs:1895-1910) returns NEW objects carrying `adjudication.upheld`, and those objects only ever reach `gating` (line 2508-2512). `writeVerdict(lensOut, lens, mergedAfter, summary, {…, gating})` at line 2648 writes verdict.json from `mergedAfter` — the pre-adjudication objects derived from `merged` (line 2492/2524), which have no `adjudication` field. The workflow builds `output.text` from verdict.json's `findings` (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:877-909, which explicitly maps `adjudication: Number.isInteger(f.adjudication?.upheld) ? … : undefined`), and review-round-guard.mjs:196-227 reads the count back from `output.text`. So the increment is discarded at the end of the round: next round's carried-forward finding arrives with no count, `upheldCount` returns 0, and `upheldTwice` never becomes true. Every promise made in this diff about "skipping the same finding twice pages a human" (agent-fix.yml prompt, review-panel.mjs:2507, fix-report.mjs:251) therefore has no effect in production; the unit test at review-panel.test.mjs:3226 only exercises the in-memory hop by feeding the annotated object straight back in. (The same gap pre-exists for `adjudicateRebuttals`, but this change newly depends on it.)

samples.summary: applySkipClaims breaks the object identity adjudicateRebuttals relies on, so an overturned finding can survive in the summary and be carried forward
samples.evidence: `adjudicateRebuttals` documents (review-panel.mjs:1943-1947) that its `dropped` array holds "the ORIGINAL objects", because the caller removes them from `merged` by identity: `mergedAfter = merged.filter((f) => !overturnedOut.has(f))` (line 2524). Inserting `applySkipClaims(gatingRaw, skipClaims)` at line 2508 replaces skip-claimed findings with `{...f, adjudication}` COPIES, so if such a finding is also matched by a rebuttal record and overturned, `dropped` contains the copy and the original stays in `mergedAfter` — it is still rendered in the check body and, worse, still persisted to `output.text` and re-raised next round, undoing the overturn. This overlap is reachable: `authorClaims`'s `covered()` (fix-report.mjs:259) compares the CLAIM's summary to the rebuttal's summary, so a rebuttal that matches the finding but whose wording drifted from the claim's is not treated as covering it; likewise a `fixed`-claim record (in `rebuttals`) can score above threshold on a finding for which a lower-scoring `skipped` claim was selected by `claimFor`. In that case `adjudicateRebuttals` also re-increments `upheld` on top of the skip increment, double-counting in a single round.

samples.summary: Fix reports are never scoped to a commit/round, so the latest report is replayed on every subsequent panel round
samples.evidence: `authorClaims` takes `latestReport(reports)` and uses it unconditionally; the record's `head` field (serialized at fix-report.mjs:100-104) is never compared against the panel's `--head-sha`, and review-panel.mjs:2191-2209 passes nothing of the kind. So one `@claude fix` report is re-applied on every later panel round for the same PR: each round `applySkipClaims` adds another `+1` to the uphold counter for the same single skip (paging a human for one skip rather than two, once the persistence gap above is fixed), and each round re-converts the same `fixed` claims into rebuttal records that buy up to MAX_FIX_ADJUDICATIONS fresh 20-turn adjudicator sessions to re-judge claims about a tree that has since changed — exactly the staleness the function's own doc comment (lines 229-236) says it prevents. The doc's reasoning ('only the latest report counts') addresses ordering between reports, not staleness relative to the current head.

samples.summary: The adjudication cap selects claims by report order, and the overflow pushes author-claimed fixes toward paging without ever being examined
samples.evidence: `fixed.slice(0, MAX_FIX_ADJUDICATIONS)` / `fixed.slice(MAX_FIX_ADJUDICATIONS)` cuts on the order the agent happened to emit `--fixed` items, with no regard to the finding's severity, so a critical claim can be deferred while a major one is adjudicated. Deferred `fixed` claims are then handed to `applySkipClaims`, which increments `adjudication.upheld` with verdict `unadjudicated-fix-claim` (review-panel.mjs:1901-1907) — i.e. a genuinely fixed finding that the fresh pass re-words is moved toward the human-paging bound with no session having looked at it.

samples.summary: The always()-gated effort/metrics steps invoke a staged path that does not exist when a pre-agent step failed, so the "posted even when the agent failed" guarantee silently does not hold
samples.evidence: `Stage the trusted agent scripts` is gated on `steps.eligible.outputs.eligible == 'true'` with the implicit `success()`, so if `Build the findings brief` (or the branch checkout / pnpm install) fails, staging is skipped and `$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-tools/metrics.mjs` never exists. Both `Record agent effort metrics` and `Post fix-agent effort comment` are gated only on `always() && eligible == 'true'`, so they run and fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; `continue-on-error: true` hides it. The comment on the effort step claims it is posted 'even when the agent failed', but for every failure before the agent step no effort comment is produced — the outcome comment then says only 'a setup step failed'.

samples.summary: The outcome comment can report ✅ pushed while the job is simultaneously marked failed
samples.evidence: In `Report the outcome`, `advanced` is evaluated before `failed`, so an agent that pushed a commit and then died (e.g. on a 429 while writing its report) produces the '✅ `@claude fix` pushed …' body, and the script then calls `core.setFailed('The fix agent failed; …')`. The maintainer sees a green success message next to a red X, with no hint that the run aborted after the push — precisely the ambiguity the effort comment was added to remove.

samples.summary: `fix-report post` exits 0 after failing to post, so a lost report is indistinguishable from a filed one at the exit-code level
samples.evidence: `cmdPost` catches the `gh pr comment` failure and `process.exit(0)`, printing only to stderr and never printing the 'posted …' line. The fixer agent is instructed to run this command in the foreground and treat completion as success (agent-fix.yml prompt), so a permissions/network failure leaves the next round with no author context and nothing in the job's status to indicate it — the same silent shape the module's own docs say the CLI exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The code is as described. `applySkipClaims` (review-panel.mjs:1895-1910) returns `{...f, adjudication}` copies and is invoked on the gating subset at review-panel.mjs:2508, before `adjudicateRebuttals`, whose `dropped` array (pushed at :1963) is consumed by the caller via object identity: `merged.filter((f) => !overturnedOut.has(f))` (:2523-2524). `gatingFindings` (:786-793) is a pure filter, so identity was previously preserved; the file's own comment (:2487-2489) and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1843-1846 state that contract explicitly. Therefore a finding that is both skip-claimed and rebuttal-matched, and then overturned, is dropped as a copy while the original survives in `mergedAfter` — which is written to verdict.json findings (:2648, :2894) and persisted by .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:877-890 into `output.text`, the next round's carry-forward, undoing the overturn; it also skews laneCounts/clusterCounts (:2629,:2634). The overlap is not guarded: `covered()` in fix-report.mjs:259-260 compares claim-vs-rebuttal text only, while claimFor (fix-report.mjs:168-189) and matchRebuttal (rebuttal.mjs:183-207) each score against the finding at the non-transitive 0.3 containment threshold (rounds.mjs:270); `deferred` fixed claims (review-panel.mjs:2195-2196) give a second overlap route. The double-increment of `adjudication.upheld` (applySkipClaims:1904 then adjudicateRebuttals:1970, read by upheldCount rebuttal.mjs:286-295 / upheldTwice :298-300) is also real. Only one sub-claim is imprecise — summary.md renders `gating` (:2902), so the finding is not re-rendered in the check body — which does not refute the persistence/carry-forward defect.

verdict.reason: The described code is present exactly as claimed. `authorClaims` (fix-report.mjs:254-256) unconditionally uses `latestReport(reports)` (fix-report.mjs:221-224) with no round/head parameter; the `head` field is serialized (fix-report.mjs:80), parsed (fix-report.mjs:123) and copied onto claims (fix-report.mjs:151) but never compared to anything — grep for `.head`/`head:` in review-panel.mjs finds no use, and the call site (review-panel.mjs:2191-2209) passes only the parsed reports plus `rebuttals`; `--head-sha` is used solely for the check-run external id (review-panel.mjs:1072-1076). `readFixReports` reads every PR comment (fix-report.mjs:427-437) and no workflow retires old report comments, so the last report persists. Replay is reachable: the panel (agent-review-panel.yml:685-691, 807) and the on-demand reviewer (agent-review-on-demand.yml:334, 369) both re-read the same comment set on every invocation, so any later round without a fresh report re-applies the stale one. Effects are real: `applySkipClaims` writes `upheld: upheldCount(f) + 1` (review-panel.mjs:1904) and `upheldTwice` pages at MAX_REBUTTAL_ROUNDS = 2 (rebuttal.mjs:298-300, count carried in rounds.mjs:415), so a single skip can drive a premature human page; and `split.adjudicate` is re-merged into `rebuttals` each round (review-panel.mjs:2196), re-buying up to MAX_FIX_ADJUDICATIONS = 5 20-turn adjudicator sessions (fix-report.mjs:218) to re-judge claims about a tree that has changed — the exact staleness the doc comment at fix-report.mjs:229-236 asserts is prevented. No guard makes this unreachable, so I cannot refute it.
